title:
Comment of Elizabeth Aaron in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15423-000
Submission Date: 10/12/2026

documents.name: 151527.txt
documents.text:
Elizabeth Aaron, Wasilla, AK.
I strongly OPPOSE the DeepGreen underwater data center in the Cook Inlet. 

Among the extensive list of negative impacts this project would have, ecological concerns are forefront in my mind. This project threatens Cook Inlet beluga whales, Stellar sea lions, and fin whales; all of which are endangered. The beluga is a geographically isolated species, making the Cook Inlet populations the only in the world.

Many other animals rely on the Cook Inlet as well, spanning marine life to birds to land animals. Otters, foxes, goats, bears, moose, bald eagles, puffins… the list goes on.

Humans rely on the ecological resources of the Cook Inlet as well for both sustenance and economic gain. Crab, clams, mussels, halibut, cod, lingcod, herring, hooligan, and more are harvested from the water. The Cook Inlet is a passageway for all five kinds of salmon. Hunters harvest land animals and fowl that visit the shores of the inlet. Tourists come from around the world to participate in whale watching tours or fishing charters in these waters, bringing valuable revenue into the state.

These data centers come with high thermal pollution, which will devastate the cold-water ecology of the inlet in an area already threatened by the most rapid warming as a result of climate change. Corrosion, anti-biofouling agents, and heavy metal leakage all contribute to environmental degradation, along with the physical disturbance of installation and maintenance of the system. When looking at the actual stability of an underwater data center, one wonders if the silty, sinking soils of the Cook Inlet even make sense in the first place. Combine this with earthquakes, intense tides, and passage of boats and ships utilizing sonar or anchors…this project is foolish and destructive on all fronts.
